original_question: When one colors copies of different finite graphs inside the Rado graph, do the resulting rainbow Ramsey theorems all have the same reverse-mathematical strength, or does that strength vary with the number of vertices in the finite graph being colored?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem (12): "How do the strengths of the rainbow Ramsey theorem for the Rado graph compare for colorings of different finite graphs? Are they all the same, or does the number of vertices in the finite graph being colored affect the strength?"
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact topic of Section 2, Problem (12): it is about the reverse-mathematical comparison of rainbow Ramsey principles for the Rado graph when the finite graph G being colored is varied, and it correctly highlights the paper's specific contrast between "all the same" and "affected by the number of vertices."
missing_details: The paper frames the question explicitly over the base system RCA0.

The relevant principle is not an unspecified "rainbow Ramsey theorem," but the Rado-graph rainbow Ramsey statement from Section 1: for a fixed finite graph G and integer k >= 2, every coloring of all copies of G in the Rado graph R into countably many colors, with each color used at most k times, has a subgraph R' of R with R' isomorphic to R such that no two copies of G in R' receive the same color.
The draft does not state that the colorings are k-bounded, i.e. each color may appear at most k times.
The draft does not state that the codomain of the coloring is omega many colors rather than finitely many colors.
The draft does not make explicit that the homogeneous object produced is a subgraph R' which is again a Rado graph.
The draft should say that one compares the reverse-mathematical strength of the formal principles obtained by fixing the finite graph G, rather than speaking loosely of "resulting theorems."

Whether k is held fixed is implicit in your draft; nearby Problem (10) treats the dependence on k as a separate question, so a stand-alone formulation should fix k >= 2 when comparing different finite graphs.
The paper's official wording asks whether the number of vertices of the finite graph being colored affects the strength; it does not ask for a broader classification beyond that dichotomy.
refined_question: Over RCA0, fix an integer k >= 2. For a finite graph G, let RR_R(G,k) be the statement that every coloring of all copies of G in the Rado graph R into countably many colors, with each color used at most k times, admits a subgraph R' subseteq R with R' isomorphic to R such that no two copies of G in R' have the same color. As G ranges over finite graphs, do the principles RR_R(G,k) all have the same reverse-mathematical strength, or can the strength vary with the number of vertices of G?
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Section 2, Problem (12), so that is the nearest official formulation in the paper. To make it stand-alone, one must import the definition of the relevant rainbow Ramsey principle from Section 1, where the paper specifies the parameters G and k, the k-bounded omega-coloring hypothesis, and the conclusion that there is a subgraph R' which is again a Rado graph and on which all copies of G get distinct colors. I fixed k >= 2 in the refined question because Section 2, Problem (10) separately asks whether the strength depends on k, so Problem (12) is most faithfully read as isolating the dependence on the finite graph parameter G rather than conflating it with the k-parameter.
